answer: False premise. PIA's Solvency II coverage ratio did not fall in 2025. It rose from 141.2% at YE2024 to 309.7% at YE2025 (after foreseeable dividends). The new reinsurance agreement with PAC took effect on 1 October 2025 and transferred significant insurance risk to PAC. It reduced profit by GBP 2.5m, but it 'significantly strengthened' the coverage ratio. The SCR fell from GBP 288.4m to GBP 138.7m, mainly through lower market risk (159.2m to 81.1m) and lower life underwriting risk (196.5m to 74.2m). Eligible own funds rose from GBP 407m to GBP 430m, after deducting GBP 65m of foreseeable 2026 dividends.

evidence.text: PIA entered a new reinsurance agreement with its parent company PAC which had the effect of reducing profit by £2.5m, but this significantly strengthened its solvency coverage ratio, which increased from 141.2% at YE24 to 309.7% (after recognition of foreseeable dividends) at YE25.
Overall, the new reinsurance results in a lower solvency capital requirement and a more balanced risk profile in 2025. ... Solvency Capital Requirement 138.7 288.4

notes: The premise is contradicted by the document. Ratio rounded inputs (430/139) give about 309%. The reported ratio is 309.7%.

answer: At 30 June 2025, the 'Short rates up' supervisory shock scenario produced the largest decrease in CBA NV's economic value of equity: EUR -965,790.94 (absolute EUR amount, about EUR 0.97 million). The next largest were Parallel up (EUR -835,493.44) and then Flattener (EUR -745,294.84). At 30 June 2024, the most adverse scenario for EVE was 'Parallel down', at EUR -679,002.25.

Footnote 10 makes the unit absolute EUR, not EUR thousand, even though the report's default unit is EUR thousand.

answer: ECB 'Liabilities related to TARGET (net)' at year-end, in EUR millions: 2021: 334,618; 2022: 315,090; 2023: 404,336 (the highest); 2024: 348,074; 2025: 313,491. The 2025 decrease was EUR 34,583 million (about EUR 34.6 billion). The ECB says it was mainly due to cash inflows from maturing APP and PEPP securities, which are settled via TARGET accounts. These inflows were partly offset by cash outflows from (i) lower deposits accepted by the ECB as fiscal agent for the European Commission (EU borrowing and lending activities), shown as a decrease in euro-denominated liabilities to non-euro area residents, and (ii) interest expense paid on the ECB's net TARGET liability.

evidence.text: The decrease in the net TARGET liability was mainly attributable to the cash inflows as a result of the maturing of securities under the APP and the PEPP, which were settled via TARGET accounts
In 2025 the ECB's net TARGET liability decreased by €34.6 billion, mainly owing to cash inflows from redemptions of monetary policy securities

notes: The five-year figures come from section 2.8 'Financial statements 2021-25' (PDF p.81, printed page 80). The layout for 2021-23 was restated for comparability. The 2025 relative change is -34,583/348,074 = -9.94%.

answer: The GFI Fund was more sensitive. At 31 December 2025, a 0.75% rise in interest rates would have reduced its net assets by USD 33,859 thousand. That is 4.50% of its net assets of USD 752,433 thousand, with an effective duration of 6.0 years. The GGI Fund's effective duration was 2.4 years, and its stated decrease was USD 667 thousand, or 1.80% of its net assets of USD 37,039 thousand.

evidence.text: As at 31 December 2025, the effective duration of the GFI Fund was 6.0 years (31 December 2024: 6.4 years) and the effective duration of GGI Fund was 2.4 years

notes: Net assets are net assets attributable to holders of redeemable participating shares, from the statement of financial position (p.16) and matching the interest-rate tables (pp.32-33). For comparison, at 31 Dec 2024 the ratios were GFI 4.80% and GGI 1.73%.
